prompt:
You transcribe images of JEE exam questions into markdown. The
transcription is stored as the question's text and must stand in for the
image: a reader of the rendered markdown should see what the printed
question says, and nothing else.

Rules:

1. Copy exactly what is printed, typos included. Do not solve, correct,
   complete or add anything. Reproduce typos and inconsistencies exactly
   as printed, even if they look like mistakes: if a series printed as
   1^3 + 2^3 + ... + n^2 looks wrong, still write n^2.
2. Approximate the layout in markdown: paragraphs and line breaks, lists
   and tables. Every labelled line (options, statements, numbered or
   lettered entries, including roman numerals) is a markdown list item
   starting with "- ", with the label as printed, e.g. "- (A) ...",
   "- (iii) ...", "- (IV) ...", "- STATEMENT 1: ...". Never write
   labelled lines as consecutive plain lines. Options printed in a grid
   go one per line, in label order.
3. Maths in LaTeX, $...$ inline and $$...$$ display. Chemistry as
   $\ce{...}$ (MathJax mhchem). No other delimiters: no \( \), no \[ \].
   Use $$...$$ only for an expression printed on its own line; words
   printed on the same line as an expression stay outside the maths.
4. Each figure is a fenced code block with the info string diagram, placed
   where the figure appears. It holds a factual description of what is
   drawn: shapes, labels, values, arrows and how the parts are arranged,
   with printed labels and values copied exactly. This block is the only
   place for anything you infer: only printed text goes outside diagram
   blocks, and names or identifications you work out (a compound's name,
   what a circuit is) go inside the block.
5. No image placeholders, and no text outside the transcription: no
   introduction, notes, explanation, answer or solution.

Notation, so that every transcription is written the same way:

- Element symbols, formulas, ions, equations and electron configurations
  in $\ce{...}$, e.g. $\ce{H2SO4}$, $\ce{Fe^{3+}}$,
  $\ce{2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O}$, $\ce{[Kr] 4d^{10} 5s^1}$.
- Function names as \sin, \cos, \tan, \ln, \log, and
  \operatorname{cosec} for cosec.
- Printed words go outside maths as plain text. Do not wrap prose in
  \text{...} inside $...$. Single letters used as labels or variables in
  an expression are maths: $a > b > c > d$.
- Units as printed, set upright after the number: $10\,\mathrm{m/s^2}$
  if the page prints m/s², $10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ if it prints m s⁻².
- Degrees as ^\circ, e.g. $30^\circ$.
- No \left and \right unless the printed brackets are visibly sized to
  their contents.
- A blank to fill in is written \_\_\_\_\_ (escaped underscores).
- Leave out the question number printed before the question, any heading
  that only names question numbers (such as "Paragraph for Questions 45
  and 46"), and any page furniture (headers, footers, watermarks, marks
  for the question).

Tables (match lists, data tables):

- One table column per printed column. A label and its text go in the
  same cell, e.g. "A. 2-Methylpropene and but-1-ene".
- All printed title lines of a column go in its header cell, e.g.
  "List-I: Pair of Compounds". Use no empty columns or rows of your own.
- If columns have different lengths, leave the missing cells empty.
- Inside a table, write a vertical bar in maths as \lvert and \rvert,
  never as |, which would break the table.

A two-column match list printed with the titles "Column I" / "Process"
and "Column II" / "Sign of ΔS" is written:

| Column I: Process | Column II: Sign of ΔS |
|---|---|
| (A) Melting of ice | (p) Positive |
| (B) Freezing of water | (q) Negative |
| | (r) Zero |

Diagram blocks:

- Plain text only inside a diagram block: no $, no LaTeX. Use Unicode
  symbols (°, θ, ², ⁻, →).
- Each drawn chemical structure gets its own diagram block, with its
  printed label if it has one, and a last line `smiles: <SMILES>`.
- Arrows, reagents and conditions printed between structures are printed
  text: write them outside the blocks, e.g. $\ce{->[AlCl3]}$ P.
- If an option or a table cell is a figure, write only its label there,
  and put the diagram block after the list or table, starting its
  description with that label, e.g. "Option (B): ..." or
  "Column I (C): ...".

A diagram block looks like this:

```diagram
A block of mass m on a smooth incline at angle θ to the horizontal,
attached by a string over a pulley at the top to a hanging mass M.
```

A structure looks like this:

```diagram
Structure (II): a cyclohexane ring carrying a COOH group.
smiles: OC(=O)C1CCCCC1
```

Reply with the transcription only, as plain markdown, not wrapped in a
code fence.

This question:

- Subject: Physics
- Type: Multiple correct answers

Multiple correct answers. Transcribe the question, then its options as a
list.

Transcribe the question in the image.

response.response:
Figure shows an incident wavefront and refracted or reflected wavefront after a single optical device -

```diagram
A curved line labeled "Incident wavefront" is on the left, concave to the right.
A horizontal arrow points to the right, below the incident wavefront.
To the right of the arrow, a vertical straight line is labeled "Refracted or reflected wave front".
```

which of the following may be the optical device-
- (A) concave lens
- (B) convex lens
- (C) concave mirror
- (D) convex mirror
